 WEST PALM BEACH Fla. (CBS12) — Inclement weather and severe flooding across South Florida could be affecting polling locations for Tuesday’s midterm elections.
 Severe weather across Palm Beach County and the Treasure Coast has caused many counties to relocate polling sites in some precincts.
 Here is a look at the polling site changes that have been made because of the unfavorable conditions:
 INDIAN RIVER COUNTY: 
 Due to flooding at the Sebastian Church of God, 281 Delaware, voters assigned to Precinct 7 will now vote at the Sebastian Elks Lodge, 2714 South Fleming St., Sebastian. The Elk’s Lodge is also the polling location for Precinct 8. Precinct 7 voters should go there for Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.
 MARTIN COUNTY: 
 Polling Precinct 2 at Grace Presbyterian Church has been relocated to the Martin County Elections Office located at: 135 SE Martin Luther King, Jr. Blvd, Stuart, FL 34994
 PALM BEACH COUNTY: 
 Voters who normally cast their ballots at Casa Rio Clubhouse in Riviera Beach will now vote at Riviera Beach Preparatory and Achievement Academy.
 Voters assigned to Ironhorse Country Club will now head to the North County Senior Center.
 ST. LUCIE COUNTY: 
 Precinct 12, originally at Fort Pierce Masonic Lodge: Days Inn Midtown, 3224 S. U.S. 1, Fort Pierce.
 Precincts 49 and 71, originally at Oak Hammock K-8 School, and Precinct 51, originally at Disabled American Veterans Hall: Port St. Lucie Community Center, 2195 SE Airoso Blvd., Port St. Lucie. Access is from Airoso Boulevard.
 Precincts 67 and 86, originally at St. Lucie West Centennial High School: Indian River State College Veterans Center of Excellence, 500 NW California Blvd., Port St. Lucie. Access is from Peacock Boulevard.
 Precinct 83, originally at Paula A. Lewis Library, and Precinct 92, originally at The Brennity at Tradition: Tradition Town Hall, 10799 SW Civic Lane, Port St. Lucie.
